title: Pointwise criterion for a nodal singularity by the first Fitting ideal
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and let $x$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points]. Let $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(C/k)$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Say that $x$ is a node when, for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and some point $\bar x$ of the base change $C_{\bar k}$ [def-pc-base-change] over $x$, the completed local ring (the $\mathfrak m_{\bar x}$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] of $\mathcal O_{C_{\bar k},\bar x}$) is isomorphic to $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] (the completed geometric local-ring condition of [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]). Then $x$ is a node if and only if the residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a finite separable algebraic extension of $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $x$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra that is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], and $\mathcal O_{Z,x}=\kappa(x)$ (equivalently, the first Fitting ideal of the relative differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] generates the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{C,x}$).

source.place: Tags 0C4D (lemma-nodal), 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), and 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), pointwise form at a closed point

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $S$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Write $\mathfrak p$ for the maximal ideal representing $x$, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$. By [lem-trf-geometric-field-stalk-descent], $F=S/\mathfrak p$ is finite over $k$, and every point of $U_{\bar k}$ over $x$ is closed with residue field $\bar k$. Write $B=(S\otimes_k\bar k)_{\mathfrak q}$ for the local ring of one such point, and $\mathfrak n$ for its maximal ideal. Let $J_A$ and $J_B$ be the respective first Fitting ideals of the differential modules. The definition of $Z$ identifies $\mathcal O_{Z,x}$ with $A/J_A$ when $x\in Z$. Thus $\mathcal O_{Z,x}=F$ via the residue map means exactly $J_A=\mathfrak m$; in particular it implies $x\in Z$.

source.place: 0C4D: affine reduction, closed residue fields and the meaning of the Fitting field-stalk condition

proof.text: Suppose that $x$ is a node, and choose the point above $x$ whose completion is $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Apply [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] to the finite-type $\bar k$-algebra $S\otimes_k\bar k$ and its rational closed point. It gives a power-series presentation of $\widehat B$ and identifies its Jacobian cokernel with $\Omega_{B/\bar k}\otimes_B\widehat B$. The node hypothesis gives only a ring isomorphism $\widehat B\cong\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$, and $uv$ has discriminant $1$ in every characteristic; so condition (c) of [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-quadratic-criterion] holds for this presentation, and implication (c) to (a) gives $\operatorname{depth}(\widehat B)=1$ and makes the ideal of the Jacobian minors its maximal ideal. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], that ideal is $J_B\widehat B$. Hence $J_B\widehat B=\mathfrak n\widehat B$.

source.place: 0C4C and 0C49: the model uv and the formal Jacobian criterion; 0C4D: algebraically closed computation

proof.text: The completion map $B\to\widehat B$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Contracting step 2 with [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] gives $J_B=\mathfrak n$. Thus $B/J_B=\bar k$. The module $\Omega_{S/k}$ is finite: if $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ generate $S$ as a $k$-algebra, repeated use of additivity and Leibniz expresses every $\mathrm ds$ as an $S$-linear combination of $\mathrm ds_i$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] with $R=k$, $R'=\bar k$, and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] at $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$, the differential modules defining $J_A$ and $J_B$ are obtained from $\Omega_{S/k}$ by the respective scalar extensions. Hence [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] identifies the base-changed first-Fitting subscheme with the singular subscheme computed over $\bar k$. Its local ring at our point is the field just computed.

source.place: 0C4D: descent from the geometric Fitting point; Algebra 00RV and 00RT for differential base change and localization

proof.text: Let $J\subset S$ be the first Fitting ideal before localization and put $T=S/J$. Step 3 shows that the image of $\mathfrak q$ defines a point of $\operatorname{Spec}(T\otimes_k\bar k)$ whose local ring is $\bar k$. Its image is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak p/J$, since $J_B\subset\mathfrak n$ implies $J\subset\mathfrak p$. The algebra $T$ is finitely generated, by the images of any finite generating set of $S$. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-field-stalk-descent] to $T$ and this point. It gives $T_{\mathfrak p/J}=F$ via the residue map and makes $F/k$ finite separable. Since $T_{\mathfrak p/J}=A/J_A$, this proves the residue-field and Fitting-stalk requirements in the forward implication.

source.place: 0C4D: arbitrary-field paragraph descending the reduced geometric singular point

proof.text: Now $F/k$ is finite separable, so [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] applies to $A$ and to the embedding $F\hookrightarrow\bar k$ determined by $\mathfrak q$. It says that $A\to B$ is flat local with closed fibre $\bar k$, and that the completion of each local ring has the same residue field as that local ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] first to $B\to\widehat B$ (flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]), then to $A\to B$, and finally to $A\to\widehat A$. In each application the closed fibre is a field and has depth $0$, since its maximal ideal is zero and no element of it is a nonzerodivisor. Thus step 2 yields $\operatorname{depth}B=\operatorname{depth}A=\operatorname{depth}\widehat A=1$.

source.place: 0C4D: flat-local depth comparison; 07NW via the depth formula

proof.text:
Use the presentation $\widehat A=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ supplied by [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation]. Its Jacobian cokernel is $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$, so [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] and step 4 make the ideal of its $(n-1)$-minors $J_A\widehat A=\mathfrak m\widehat A$. Together with depth one from step 5, [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-quadratic-criterion] gives $\widehat A\cong F[[u,v]]/(Q)$ with $Q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ and $b^2-4ac
e0$. In particular $Q
e0$. Its multiplication on $F[[u,v]]$ is injective: under the total-degree-then-lexicographic order, the least nonzero monomial of a product of two nonzero series is the product of their least nonzero monomials and has nonzero coefficient. Also $Q\in(u,v)$, so $(Q)$ is a regular sequence. By [lem-trf-completion-local-complete-intersection], some $S_g$, $g
otin\mathfrak p$, is a local complete intersection over $k$. The principal open $\operatorname{Spec}S_g\subset U\subset C$ is the required affine neighbourhood of $x$.

source.place: 0C4C/0C49 followed by 0C4E: formal quadratic hypersurface gives the affine LCI neighbourhood

proof.text: For the converse, choose the assumed affine local-complete-intersection neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $x$, and retain $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ and $F=S/\mathfrak p$. The hypotheses give finite separability of $F/k$ and $J_A=\mathfrak m$. By [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] with $O=C$ and $n=1$, the local topological dimension of $C$ at $x$ is $1$. This is also the dimension at $x$ in its open neighbourhood $U$: the open neighbourhoods contained in $U$ are cofinal among the open neighbourhoods of $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring], $\dim A=1$. The depth conclusion of [lem-trf-completion-local-complete-intersection], applied to the LCI algebra $S$, therefore gives $\operatorname{depth}A=1$.

source.place: 0C4E: LCI implies Cohen-Macaulay, and dimension at a closed point is one

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] to $A$. Its completion is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ and residue field $F$. Its completion map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] and the field closed fibre give $\operatorname{depth}\widehat A=\operatorname{depth}A=1$. In its formal presentation, the differential-cokernel comparison in the presentation node and [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] identify the Jacobian-minor ideal with $J_A\widehat A=\mathfrak m\widehat A$. Therefore [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-quadratic-criterion] gives a complete local $F$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat A\cong F[[u,v]]/(Q)$ with $Q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ and $b^2-4ac\ne0$.

source.place: 0C4D: the depth-one Fitting condition gives the nondegenerate quadratic completion

proof.text: By [lem-trf-geometric-field-stalk-descent], there is a geometric point over $x$ with residue field $\bar k$. Its residue map determines an embedding $F\hookrightarrow\bar k$. The base-change clause of [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation], applied to the quadratic presentation just obtained (a continuous $F$-algebra surjection $F[[u,v]]\to\widehat A$ for the section of step 8, with $n=2$ and kernel $(Q)\subseteq(u,v)$), gives $\widehat B\cong\bar k[[u,v]]/(Q)$. Over the algebraically closed field $\bar k$, the binary quadratic $Q$ factors as a scalar times two linear forms. The forms are distinct and linearly independent: if they were proportional, $Q$ would be a square up to scalar and its discriminant would vanish, including in characteristic $2$. A change to these two linear coordinates and absorption of the nonzero scalar consequently identify this quotient with $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. This is the required geometric nodal completion, proving the converse.

source.place: 0C49 and 0C4D: extend the nondegenerate binary quadratic to the algebraic closure and split it

split_report.summary: Retained the statement and split it into nine steps following Stacks 0C4D/0C4C/0C4E. Four genuine general auxiliary statements record the formal Jacobian quadratic criterion, separable closed-point formal and differential comparisons, geometric field-stalk descent, and the completion criterion for LCI neighbourhoods with its depth consequence. Existing nodes supply Fitting base change, faithful-flat contraction, the local depth formula and closed-point dimension. The proof explicitly descends the geometric singular field stalk before using a separable coefficient field.

lean.statement: theorem nodalPoint_iff_separable_lci_firstFitting {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hpure : C.IsPureDimension 1) (x : C) (hx : x ∈ closedPoints C) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosure k Ω] : (∃ y : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω))), pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω))) y = x ∧ Nonempty (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω)))).presheaf.stalk y)) ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω)))).presheaf.stalk y) ≃+* (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) Ω ⧸ Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) Ω) * (MvPowerSeries.X 1 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) Ω)}))) ↔ (f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x).Finite ∧ @Algebra.IsSeparable k (C.residueField x) _ _ (f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x).toAlgebra ∧ ∃ (U : C.affineOpens) (hxU : x ∈ U.1) (hfg : @Algebra.FiniteType k Γ(C, U.1) _ _ ((f.appLE ⊤ U.1 le_top).hom.comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom).toAlgebra), @Algebra.IsLocalCompleteIntersection k Γ(C, U.1) _ _ ((f.appLE ⊤ U.1 le_top).hom.comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom).toAlgebra hfg ∧ ((Scheme.firstFittingIdealSheaf f).ideal U).map (C.presheaf.germ U.1 x hxU).hom = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk x)
